WITH categorized_cycles AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT 
        tcs.item_id,
        tcs.version,
        tcs.teams_set,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name LIKE '%SME%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS sme,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name LIKE '%Golden%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS gdb,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name LIKE '%Automated%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS automated,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name NOT LIKE '%Automated%' AND tcs.cycle_short_name NOT LIKE '%Golden%' and tcs.cycle_short_name NOT LIKE '%SME%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS manual
    FROM athena.mv_test_cycle_statistics tcs
    WHERE 
        tcs.cycle_name LIKE '%Regression%' 
        AND tcs.project_code = 'DEMO' 
        AND tcs.version = '$versions'
        AND item_execution_rank = 1
)
SELECT 
    t.version,
    SUM(t.automated) AS "Automated",
    SUM(t.manual) AS "Manual",
    SUM(t.gdb) AS "Dev Automated",
    SUM(t.sme) AS "SME"
FROM categorized_cycles t
GROUP BY t.version
ORDER BY SUM(t.automated + t.manual + t.gdb)

options.content:
What this chart shows:

This chart displays both the percentage and number of test cases in the selected Regression cycle, grouped by team and categorized into three types:
  • Automated: Tests that run automatically without human involvement.
  • Manual: Tests that require a person to execute.
  • GDB: Unit-test-like functional tests related to Golden Database validation.

Why it matters:

  • Helps us understand testing efficiency and workload distribution across teams.
  • A higher GDB and Automated percentage often indicates a healthier quality engineering process and reduced risk.
  • Important to note: some manual tests are intentionally not automated due to complexity or business needs.
  • A higher number of manual tests can mean more effort and longer regression cycles.

How to interpret:

  • Higher percentages often (but not always) reflect more effective teams in delivering features.
  • 100% Automated + GDB means no regression and low risk for that team.
  • Example: If a team shows 120 Automated and 5 Manual, it means they mostly rely on automation but still perform some manual checks and might need couple of hours to wrap each iteration.

WITH categorized_cycles AS (

        tcs.version,
        COALESCE(tcs.teams_set->>0, '--') as team,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name LIKE '%Golden%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS gdb,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name LIKE '%Automated%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS automated,
        CASE 
            WHEN tcs.cycle_short_name NOT LIKE '%Automated%' AND tcs.cycle_short_name NOT LIKE '%Golden%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 
        END AS manual
    FROM athena.mv_test_cycle_statistics tcs
    WHERE 
        tcs.cycle_name LIKE '%Regression%' 
        AND tcs.project_code = 'DEMO' 
        AND tcs.version = '$versions'
        AND item_execution_rank = 1
)
SELECT 
    replace(t.team, 'Team ',''),
    SUM(t.automated) AS automated,
    SUM(t.manual) AS manual,
    SUM(t.gdb) AS gdb
FROM categorized_cycles t
Where t.team not in ('Mobile', 'Performance', 'SME team')
GROUP BY t.team
ORDER BY t.team

What this chart shows:

This chart visualizes the cumulative execution percentage of test cases over time for each Regression test cycle. It helps track progress hour by hour, showing how quickly each cycle is approaching completion.
  • Time Axis: Represents hourly intervals during the regression cycle.
  • Value: Percentage of executed tests compared to total planned tests.
  • Series: Each line represents a different test cycle.

Why it matters:

  • Shows real-time progress and cumulative execution trends.
  • Helps identify cycles that are lagging behind or progressing well.
  • Higher percentages indicate faster execution and better adherence to timelines.

How to interpret:

  • A steady upward trend means consistent progress toward completion.
  • Flat lines indicate no execution activity during that time window.
  • Example: If Cycle A reaches 80% by mid-day, it means most tests are executed and the cycle is close to completion.

▶ SCROLL Legends to find missing cycles and set time range on the dashboard level to explore detailed time intervals.

targets.rawSql:
WITH daily AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('hour', executed_on) AS hour,
        cycle_short_name AS "Test Cycle",
        SUM(pass + "blocked" + in_progress + fail) / MAX(cycle_size)::float * 100 AS "Total Executed"
    FROM athena.mv_test_cycle_statistics
    WHERE cycle_name LIKE '%Regression%' 
      AND project_code = 'DEMO' 
      AND version = '$versions'
      AND cycle_name NOT LIKE '%Automated%' and cycle_name NOT LIKE '%SME%'
      AND executed_on IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('hour', executed_on), cycle_short_name
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(hour, NOW()) AS "time",
    "Test Cycle" AS metric,
    SUM("Total Executed") OVER (
        PARTITION BY "Test Cycle"
        ORDER BY COALESCE(hour, NOW())
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS value
FROM daily
ORDER BY "time", "Test Cycle";

WITH daily AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('hour', executed_on) AS hour,
        cycle_short_name AS "Test Cycle",
        SUM(pass + "blocked" + fail) / MAX(cycle_size)::float * 100 AS "Total Executed"
    FROM athena.mv_test_cycle_statistics
    WHERE cycle_name LIKE '%Regression%' 
      AND project_code = 'DEMO' 
      AND version = '$versions'
      AND cycle_short_name LIKE '%Automated%' 
      AND executed_on IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('hour', executed_on), cycle_short_name
)
SELECT
    COALESCE(hour, NOW()) AS "time",
    "Test Cycle" AS metric,
    SUM("Total Executed") OVER (
        PARTITION BY "Test Cycle"
        ORDER BY COALESCE(hour, NOW())
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS value
FROM daily
ORDER BY "time", "Test Cycle";

What these charts show:

These two charts illustrate how test cases are distributed across different test cycles for both manual and automated executions. Each cycle represents a specific phase or focus area in the testing process.

Why it matters:

Understanding this distribution helps us see how tests are spread across various functional or risk-based cycles. This ensures that critical areas receive the right level of attention during regression and hardening phases.

How to interpret:

Since we follow a risk-based testing approach, different tests are executed in different cycles based on their importance and risk level. For example, high-risk features might appear more in hardening cycles, while broader coverage happens during regression.

What this table shows:

This table displays regression execution status by team, including test case counts for each team. It breaks down execution type (manual or automated), giving a clear view of progress and coverage.

Why it matters:

It provides visibility into how regression efforts are distributed across teams and how close the team is to finzalize thier commitments.

How to interpret:

Since we follow a risk-based testing approach, execution dynamic may vary by team. High-risk areas often needs more effort and may still require manual validation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    team AS team,
    sum(CASE WHEN cycle_short_name LIKE '%Golden%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS gdb,
    sum(CASE WHEN cycle_short_name LIKE '%Automated%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS automated,
    sum(CASE WHEN cycle_name NOT LIKE '%Automated%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS manual,
    SUM(pass) AS "Pass",
    SUM(fail) AS "Fail",
    SUM(skipped) AS "Skipped",
    SUM(blocked) AS "Blocked",
    SUM(in_progress) AS "InProgress",
    SUM(unexecuted) AS "Unexecuted",
    SUM(in_progress + unexecuted) AS "Total Unexecuted",
    COUNT(*) - SUM(in_progress + unexecuted) AS "Total Executed",
    SUM(total) AS "Total"
FROM athena.mv_test_cycle_statistics
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements_text(teams_set) AS team
WHERE cycle_name LIKE '%Regression%' 
  AND project_code = 'DEMO' 
  AND version = '$versions'
  AND item_execution_rank = 1
GROUP BY team
ORDER BY team
LIMIT 10000

What this table shows:

This table lists test case counts for various functional areas within the application, broken down by execution type (manual or automated) and associated execution status. Each row represents a specific functional area.

Why it matters:

It provides visibility into how testing efforts are distributed across different parts of the application. This helps ensure that all critical areas receive adequate coverage during regression and hardening phases.

How to interpret:

Since we follow a risk-based testing approach, different functional areas may have varying levels of risk impact. While generally, a high-risk area might have more automated tests for faster feedback, it is still possible that some complex areas may still require manual checks.
